system.summary: One-part Polish code in shuffled letter blocks (key ZbPop 444 'Cyfra polska', 8 Mar 1783): groups 1-1969 for letters, syllables, endings, words and names, signal group 2345, nulls from 1970; half-marked groups (136 1/2 = Nas).
system.notes: Other systems in the same volume (tables 9933, 3865, 12282; the 1789-91 code with leading 4000) are not read here.

prior_solution.where: The cabinet's clear texts of 1786-87 are in AGAD AKP 1/11/0/-/269 (header index: a clear of the same date for 8 of the 14 pieces; none for p13, p21, p28, p33, g1, g3); not opened by the reading agent. No edition of 1786-87 (the IH PAN edition stops at 1782). Catalogue 416 open; no target on origin/main (GitHub API, 6 Nov 2026).

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout obtained the scans, set the rules (protocols hashed before each step, threshold fixed in advance, clears of the time kept unopened) and answered blind shape plates on single digits (shapes only). AI agents transcribed the key and the despatches, tested the key, read and summarised. No human palaeographer checked the transcription or the readings.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: Key of the time ZbPop 444 'Cyfra polska' (8 Mar 1783) found and transcribed in full (1,965 entries); identified as the older code of 1783-88, not the 1789-91 code.
Key tested on three 1788 despatches with the cabinet's clears (ciphers hashed first): 0.874, 0.874, held-out 0.837; criterion >= 0.90 fixed in advance: failed; controls 0.08-0.12.
ZbPop 3 sorted by opening group (444 = 22 pieces; 9933, 3865, 12282, 4000); 14 pieces in code 444 transcribed.
14 pieces read by sense, blind to the clears: 7040 words, 5499 certain, 256 probable, 4 restored, 1281 unresolved (81.8%); blind shape plates Z3a and Z3G applied.
Full-texts audit: a summary added to each of the 14 outcome.texts entries, condensed from the English summaries of translation.md (5-6 Nov 2026, from the readings); nothing new was read.

outcome.method_basis: Read with the key of the time ZbPop 444, transcribed from its scans; the key was tested on 1788 pairs and failed our 0.90 threshold (0.837), so every piece is offered as a partial reading explained.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Daniel's rule (certain + probable; restored words excluded), counted by script on reading/*.md: 7040 words, 5499 certain, 256 probable, 4 restored, 1281 unresolved = 5755/7036 = 81.8%; per piece 0.696-0.905.

validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered test of the key of the time on three 1788 despatches with the cabinet's clears (ciphers hashed before the clears): read by sense 0.874, 0.874 and 0.837 on the held-out pair (0.864 overall), against shuffled-key controls with maxima 0.08-0.12 (computation still running); criterion >= 0.90 fixed in advance: failed at that threshold; 444 confirmed as the key of 1783-88.

texts.label: piece p01, Deboli, 29 Dec 1786 (received 9 Jan 1787)

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 5-6 Nov 2026 by AI agents only, blind to the clears of the time; 316 certain, 42 probable, 0 restored, 72 unresolved of 430 words (83.3%); read in part.

texts.summary: Ostermann's evasive answer about the Russian regiments stationed in Poland kept Deboli from asking formally; he sees that Russia is not disposed to withdraw them and will press again at the next conference, arguing that the Emperor, travelling to Kiev, will see them with his own eyes.

texts.label: piece p04, Deboli, 9 Jan 1787

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 5-6 Nov 2026 by AI agents only, blind to the clears of the time; 216 certain, 18 probable, 4 restored, 99 unresolved of 337 words (70.3%); read in part.

texts.summary: Deboli expects an answer tomorrow on the King's letter about the regiment. Joseph II will come to Kherson rather than Kiev; Potemkin will receive the Empress at Krichev and Kiev; the affair of the Princess of Württemberg troubles the grand-ducal couple.

texts.label: piece p07, Deboli, 18 Jan 1787

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 5-6 Nov 2026 by AI agents only, blind to the clears of the time; 1786 certain, 25 probable, 0 restored, 418 unresolved of 2229 words (81.2%); read in part.

texts.summary: A talk with Ostermann, who refuses the withdrawal of the Russian regiment and blames Deboli's vehemence. Deboli thinks everything depends on Potemkin, fears the Commission he wants, and suggests the King write to him before Kiev; then the affair of the Palatine of Ruthenia and a castellan's son come without leave or passport.

texts.label: piece p13, Deboli, 27 Jul 1787

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 5-6 Nov 2026 by AI agents only, blind to the clears of the time; 133 certain, 14 probable, 0 restored, 51 unresolved of 198 words (74.2%); read in part.

texts.summary: Foreign ministers await an audience; the Empress received three of them at Tsarskoye Selo in very good humour. Hetman Branicki and his wife are to come to St Petersburg this winter, and there are hopes he will regain the King's favour.

texts.label: piece p15, Deboli, 31 Aug 1787

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 5-6 Nov 2026 by AI agents only, blind to the clears of the time; 219 certain, 8 probable, 0 restored, 42 unresolved of 269 words (84.4%); read in part.

texts.summary: Three posts came with no letter. The answer to the King's letter will come from the Empress herself. The British envoy has left; Ségur's tragedy 'Coriolan' was staged at the Hermitage; Ségur leaves within a week with the Prince de Ligne.

texts.label: piece p21, Deboli, 17 Aug 1787

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 5-6 Nov 2026 by AI agents only, blind to the clears of the time; 168 certain, 3 probable, 0 restored, 53 unresolved of 224 words (76.3%); read in part.

texts.summary: Deboli asks how the King's letter and its allegorical idea were received. The Empress came back to town, attended the Preobrazhensky regiment's feast at the Summer Palace and moved into the Winter Palace.

texts.label: piece p23, Deboli, 14 Sep 1787

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 5-6 Nov 2026 by AI agents only, blind to the clears of the time; 489 certain, 2 probable, 0 restored, 155 unresolved of 646 words (76.0%); read in part.

texts.summary: A courier to Warsaw; Cobenzl and the Austrian courier; the Turks have declared war; French mediation; Ostermann on France and Berlin; Prussian recruitment; the Prince de Ligne wishes to write to the King.

texts.label: piece p28, Deboli, 25 Sep 1787

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 5-6 Nov 2026 by AI agents only, blind to the clears of the time; 217 certain, 3 probable, 0 restored, 39 unresolved of 259 words (84.9%); read in part.

texts.summary: Back from Gatchina. Cobenzl says the alliance binds the Emperor to war; the Council debates peace with the Turks; Ligne's letter goes with the Austrian courier and he asks about an extraordinary Sejm.

texts.label: piece p30, Deboli, 3 Aug 1787

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 5-6 Nov 2026 by AI agents only, blind to the clears of the time; 147 certain, 17 probable, 0 restored, 48 unresolved of 212 words (77.4%); read in part.

texts.summary: Wielhorski has arrived on business of the castellan's wife Ogińska (probable) and Deboli has introduced him. Starosta Potocki would have lost 200,000 roubles in merchants' failures had they not been withdrawn, and still loses through the exchange rate.

texts.label: piece p33, Deboli, 7 Oct 1787

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 5-6 Nov 2026 by AI agents only, blind to the clears of the time; 491 certain, 22 probable, 0 restored, 54 unresolved of 567 words (90.5%); read in part.

texts.summary: Before tomorrow's conference: Rumyantsev's division has entered Turkish territory to screen Poland; Deboli will ask when to expect the answer on the alliance project. His three conclusions: Russia wants a short war (take Ochakov, then peace), the Emperor will do little at first, and a Franco-Russian union is hard.

texts.label: piece p37, Deboli, 16 Oct 1787 (the part in code 444 only)

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 5-6 Nov 2026 by AI agents only, blind to the clears of the time; 612 certain, 43 probable, 0 restored, 70 unresolved of 725 words (90.3%); read in part.

texts.summary: A long talk with Markov: Russia still wants to shield Poland in this war and come to an agreement, but will not guarantee a territory for Poland; the aim should be keeping, not enlarging, the country. Deboli answers that Russian inaction would be read as abandonment. The rest of the piece is in other tables and not read.

texts.label: piece g1, Gołuchowski, 13 Feb 1787

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 5-6 Nov 2026 by AI agents only, blind to the clears of the time; 105 certain, 10 probable, 0 restored, 30 unresolved of 145 words (79.3%); read in part.

texts.summary: Gołuchowski has nothing to add on the Empress's journey. He denies the report about Prince Repnin; Buchholtz is said to have announced the entry of 10 Russian regiments, causing alarm in Warsaw.

texts.label: piece g3, Gołuchowski, 30 Mar 1787

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 5-6 Nov 2026 by AI agents only, blind to the clears of the time; 118 certain, 10 probable, 0 restored, 56 unresolved of 184 words (69.6%); read in part.

texts.summary: At court the foreign ministers pressed him about the 10 regiments said to be entering Poland; he answered he had nothing certain. The Danish minister asked about Şahin Giray; he said he knew no more than the Hamburg papers.

texts.label: piece g4, Gołuchowski, 18 May 1787

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 5-6 Nov 2026 by AI agents only, blind to the clears of the time; 482 certain, 39 probable, 0 restored, 94 unresolved of 615 words (84.7%); read in part.

texts.summary: Asked to find out Grand Duke Paul's taste in saddle horses to be sent from Poland, Gołuchowski reports the riding master's requirements: calm, unafraid of firing and cannon, lively, sound and strong; he doubts one horse can have all these qualities and that it can arrive in time.

outcome.notes: A partial reading explained, published at Brice Dudout's request: no piece reaches 95%; for 8 of the 14 pieces a clear of the time probably exists in AKP 269 (kept unopened), so their content is probably existing and our reading is blind; the reading of the other six is new, in part. The key is of the time; the transcription is ours (CC BY 4.0).
